sentences: Your fingers don't wrinkle because they soak up water.
If they did, your whole body would wrinkle. It doesn't.
The real cause is your nerves.
After a few minutes underwater, they send a signal to the blood vessels in your fingertips.
Those vessels squeeze tight. The fingertip shrinks, and the skin on top folds into ridges.
Scientists noticed the proof back in the nineteen thirties: fingers with damaged nerves don't wrinkle, even after a long soak.
So why does your body do it? Grip.
In a twenty thirteen study, people moved wet marbles faster with wrinkled fingers.
Scientists think the ridges work like tire treads, channeling water away.
Your fingers don't soak. They switch to rain tires.
